blogs.title: The 5-Day Heuristic: Why Your Pre-Procedure Heparin Matters
blogs.description: Post-operative HIT is typically expected post-day 5, but this case challenges the timeline. Explore the implications of pre-procedure heparin exposure from cardiac catheterization and how to stratify diagnosis in patients with unusually early onset thrombocytopenia following surgery.

blogs.title: Decoding the 'Indeterminate' SRA: Patterns of Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: Not all HIT Serotonin Release Assays are created equal. Analyze the unique serological profile of autoimmune HIT (aHIT) with heparin-independent activation, particularly focusing on resistance to Fc receptor blockade and supporting evidence for diagnosis beyond the standard ELISA.

blogs.title: Beyond Platelets: Using Fibrinogen and D-Dimer to Uncover HIT Severity
blogs.description: In severe HIT, platelet lysis may be insufficient for diagnosis without other metrics. Investigate the clinical utility of falling fibrinogen and rising D-dimer levels as early markers of consumptive coagulopathy in high-risk patients, particularly when classic signs like schistocytes are absent or equivocal.

blogs.title: Anticoagulant Agnosticism: Argatroban vs. Fondaparinux in Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: When standard heparin blindness fails, which direct anticoagulant is best? Review the specific rationale for switching from direct thrombin inhibitors (Argatroban) to Factor Xa inhibitors (Fondaparinux) in the setting of severe autoimmune HIT with ongoing hypercoagulability and consumptive coagulopathy.

blogs.title: The Stroke Climax: Managing Neurological Complications in HIT
blogs.description: A stroke may be the first clue to HIT. Discuss the critical balance of anticoagulation in a HIT patient with acute cerebral infarction, weighing the risk of re-infarction against the bleeding risk of invasive management or the loss of neural plasticity from delayed treatment.

blogs.title: Antibody Decay: Long-Term Immune Tracking in Autoimmune HIT
blogs.description: Recovery of platelets does not always mean recovery of antibodies. Examine the timeline for the waning of heparin-independent antibodies in aHIT patients and the implications for long-term anticoagulation strategies once thrombocytopenia and neurological symptoms have resolved.
